breadth_audit._purpose: Makes the actor-attribution correction observable and catches regression. publishers_excluded is exact; contrast count best-effort. median_breadth_30d drives threshold re-tune.
breadth_audit.contrast_comentions_excluded: agent estimate: ~6 (GLM-5.2-vs-Claude-vs-GPT roundups kept only subject org per topic)

config_snapshot._purpose: exact tuning constants in effect this run, for reproducibility

source_weights._comment: Per-mention contribution. Higher = stronger signal. Tune by raising weights for sources you trust more.

convergence_multiplier._comment: When a topic appears in N or more DIFFERENT source types, score is multiplied. Counters monoculture (single-source loud day) and rewards cross-source agreement.

sector_config._comment: Dynamic sectors (radar quadrants) — recomputed every run based on what's actually active. Sectors carry over from yesterday's radar unless hysteresis rules trigger a change. This is what makes it a TREND radar (sectors evolve) rather than a fixed taxonomy. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if I had this earlier, we had only Models / RAG, and now from RAG we went to Agents, that's why I say it needs to be flexible.'
sector_config._clustering_method: LLM clusters topics into themes by reading topic labels + supporting context. Prior run's sectors are passed in as starting point — clusterer keeps them when membership is stable, splits/merges/renames only when warranted. The topic_taxonomy_seed group keys above are initial hints, NOT enforced labels.
sector_config._starter_sectors_comment: Used only on the very first radar run when no prior sectors exist. After that, the clusterer evolves them. If sectors get stuck for too long, manually clearing prior_sectors in the most recent radar JSON forces a fresh cluster.

breadth_config._comment: Cross-source breadth — orthogonal to the EMA-based persistence score. Answers 'how many distinct organizations are talking about this right now?' as a primary, visible dimension. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if many companies are talking or writing about the same topic, this means high-weighted related, should be seen easier.'
breadth_config._org_definition: An 'org' is an ACTOR in the topic — an organization that shipped/announced it, adopted/deployed it, regulates it, is hiring for it, or is directly and specifically affected by it. NOT a messenger (a publisher reporting the story) and NOT a contrast co-mention (a competitor named only for comparison in a roundup). The radar skill applies the actor test per mention; ambiguous cases are EXCLUDED (breadth should under-count, not inflate). For backfill where org data isn't separately stored, breadth is approximated by distinct (source_type, file_date) pairs in the window.
breadth_config._attribution_comment: Breadth counts ACTORS, not messengers or contrast co-mentions. An org counts toward a topic only when it is the subject acting on the topic. Publishers reporting the story and competitors named only for comparison do NOT count. See ai-trend-radar/SKILL.md §4 'actor test'.
breadth_config._publisher_comment: Slugs here are tech-press / analyst publishers and individual commentators — messengers, excluded from breadth counts but STILL kept in source_mentions for transparency. A publisher slug counts toward breadth ONLY if the publisher is itself the subject (e.g. an NZZ story ABOUT NZZ building RAG).
breadth_config._finance_press_note: Banks (macquarie, bnp, goldman, gvc, etc.) count toward breadth ONLY when they are the actor (deploying / investing / issuing a mandate), never when quoted as analysts in a market-reaction story.

thresholds._comment: Lowered 2026-06-03 from 15/20 alongside BREADTH_PLAN actor-attribution. Removing publishers + contrast co-mentions shrinks every topic's org set, so the old 15/20 floor (set against the inflated distribution) would almost never fire. After the first corrected radar run, read breadth_audit.median_breadth_30d and re-tune: high_breadth_7d ~= top-third of the NEW distribution, very_high ~= top-quartile.
